Maria (Support): FYI customer acme-prod opened a high-priority ticket: p99 latency up ~3x since yesterday deploy, affecting inference endpoints. They see timeouts and some 5xxs.
Alex (Oncall): Ack. Can you paste their exact timestamps and example request IDs?
Maria (Support): Sure. Start ~2026-03-14T18:20Z. Example req ids: rq_9a8b7c, rq_9a8b8. They say p95 looks OK but p99 and tail latency exploded.
Leo (CSM): Customer is threatening to route traffic off our hosted API if this drags on. Need quick mitigation.
Alex (Oncall): I pulled traces for rq_9a8b7c — looks like backend inference step had a big stall, service "runtime-gpu-1" host h12.
Jia (SRE): Before we dive deep, where are you looking for p99? Grafana panel or raw Prom? Different panels use different derivations.
Sam (Observability): Good point. The customer-facing dashboard (dash: /d/latency/production) shows p99 from a per-minute rollup metric we store in influx. The oncall panel uses direct Prom histogram aggregation. They won't match if rollup window differs.
Alex (Oncall): Can you show the Prom query you used?
Sam (Observability): Prom query I ran: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))` — that's the raw histogram approach. The dashboard rollup uses `quantiles(99)` computed during ingest over 1m buckets and then we roll that up hourly with a weighted sampler.
Maria (Support): So one says p99=1200ms, other shows 350ms for same time window. Which is correct? Customer's telemetry matches the Prom raw p99.
Jia (SRE): Two plausible sources: 1) rollup uses summary-style quantiles which underestimates tail when data is sparse or when outliers are clipped; 2) histogram buckets in Prom are coarse (we use 10ms, 50ms, 200ms, 1s, 5s), staircasing can move the quantile.
Alex (Oncall): I also noticed our rollup service had a config change on 2026-03-14 18:15Z — it switched aggregation window from 1m -> 5m for cost reasons.
Sam (Observability): Bingo. That change would smooth spikes and produce lower p99 in the rollup. The raw histogram (5m rate) still shows the spike because it's counting bucket increases across the 5m window.
Maria (Support): Customer insists raw p99 is what matters. They measure per-request latencies client-side.
Jia (SRE): For immediate mitigation: We can 1) rollback rollup window to 1m (undo change), 2) add a temporary alert on Prom raw p99 for this customer route, 3) route their traffic to a lighter model variant or dedicated pool. Which do we want now?
Alex (Oncall): Action plan: I will open an incident and trigger rollback for rollup window to 1m. Jia, can you check host h12 health and try a targeted restart if necessary? Sam, add a raw p99 alert that fires at 1.5x baseline. Maria, keep CS updated and ask acme to throttle non-critical traffic.
Jia (SRE): On it. Quick host check: `ssh h12` shows high GPU mem usage and one process with long stuck GPU kernel. Crash log snippet: ```
I0325 18:21:03 runtime.cpp:452] kernel_launch: seq=1024 dur=31.2s
E0325 18:21:03 runtime.cpp:480] stuck on kernel id 0x7ff
```
Jia (SRE): I'm going to rotate traffic off h12 for that shard. Patching now.
Sam (Observability): Adding raw alert rule: `expr=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, route)) > 1.2` — will scope to route=acme-prod.
Alex (Oncall): Incident created INC-1029, linked to customer ticket. Rolling back rollup change to 1m now. deploy-bot: can you confirm job `rollup-ingest` rollback?
deploy-bot: Rollback started for job rollup-ingest, target config: aggregation_window=1m. CI/CD link: https://ci.internal/rollups/2345
Incident-bot: INC-1029 assigned to Alex, priority=P1, started 2026-03-14T18:28Z.
Maria (Support): Customer acknowledged throttling non-critical jobs. Thanks.
Jia (SRE): Rotated shard off h12. Observed new requests land on h14/h15. Early traces for rq_9a8b8 now show typical ~200ms.
Sam (Observability): After rollback, rollup p99 aligned closer to Prom raw within ~2% in the 30m window. Looks like the config change was the main cause.
Alex (Oncall): Good. Longer-term we need to: a) enforce rollup change review process for tail-sensitive metrics, b) store both raw histogram rollups and summary quantiles or include max/99th samples to avoid smoothing issues. I'll add to backlog.
Maria (Support): Customer is satisfied with temporary mitigation and will watch for one more day before closing ticket.
Leo (CSM): I'll send them a summary and propose a dedicated capacity pilot if they need firm SLOs.
Jia (SRE): One note: even with rollback, we still saw occasional true backend stalls (the stuck GPU kernel). I'll file a follow-up to investigate kernel hangs and model runtime stability.
Sam (Observability): Recorded dashboard change and created playbook doc: "How rollup windows affect p95/p99" — link: https://docs.internal/obs/rollup-p99 (will add examples and recommended defaults).
Alex (Oncall): Closing incident once customer confirms. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Maria (Support): Closing loop with customer. :white_check_mark:
